Surah Maryam (the chapter of Maryam, the Mary) [Makkiyyah (revealed in Makkah) except its prostration verse, and then Madaniyyah (revealed in Madinah) or, except "fa-khalafa min ba'dihim khalf" (﴿Then there succeeded them an evil generation﴾) the two verses, and then they are Madaniyyatan (two Madinan verses). It has 98 or 99 verses. It was revealed after Surah Fatir.]

﴿Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ﴾ — "This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti): ﴿ذِكْرُ﴾ (the mention, i.e., the account) — the object of "mercy" (raḥmah) is ﴿زَكَرِيَّا﴾ (Zakariyya, Zechariah), which serves as an explanatory apposition (bayān) for "His servant" (ʿabdahu).

﴿When﴾ relates to "mercy" (in the previous verse): ﴿he called upon his Lord with a call﴾ containing a supplication, ﴿secretly﴾, in private, in the depth of the night, because it is more likely to be answered.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 4:

﴿He said: "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened﴾ (waha, i.e., became feeble) ﴿all of them, within me; and my head has flared up﴾ within me ﴿with white hair﴾ (shayban), a specification (tamyiz) transferred from the subject; meaning, the grey hair has spread through his hair the way the spark of fire spreads through firewood. And indeed I wish to call upon You﴾ ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You﴾, meaning: in my supplication to You, ﴿my Lord﴾ (rabb), ﴿unsuccessful﴾ (shaqiyyan), meaning: disappointed in what has passed, so do not disappoint me in what is to come.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 5:

﴿And indeed I fear the mawali (mawali) after me﴾, i.e., those who are close to me in lineage, such as the paternal cousins, ﴿from behind me﴾, i.e., after my death, regarding the religion, that they will neglect it, as I have witnessed among the Children of Israel in the alteration of the religion. ﴿And my wife has been barren﴾, not bearing children, ﴿so grant me from Yourself﴾, from Your presence, ﴿an heir (waliyyan)﴾, a son.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 19, verse 6:**

﴿who will inherit me﴾, in the jussive (*jazm*, the mood that drops the final vowel) as an answer to the imperative, and in the nominative (*raf'*) as an attribute (*ṣifa*) of *waliyyan* (وَلِيًّا). ﴿and inherit﴾ may be read with either of the two forms. ﴿from the family of Ya'qub﴾, my grandfather of knowledge and prophethood. ﴿And make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾, i.e., *marḍiyyan* (مَرْضِيًّا), pleasing in Your sight. Allah the Exalted said, in answering his request, the son through whom His mercy was realized.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, a classical *tafsir* [Qur'anic exegesis]) on surah 19, verse 7:

﴿O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy﴾ who will inherit as you asked, ﴿whose name is Yahya; We have not made any namesake for him before﴾, i.e., named Yahya.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 8:

﴿He said, "My Lord, how⦅?⦆ ﴾ how (kayfa) ﴿can I have a boy, when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age, a decrepitude﴾ from ʿataa (ʿataa): it dried up, i.e., the extreme limit of age, one hundred and twenty years, and his wife had reached ninety-eight years.

The original form of ʿitiyyan (عِتِيًّا) is ʿitiwwan (عِتِوّ). The kasra on the taa' was dropped for lightness, and the first waw was changed to a yaa' to match the kasra, and the second became a yaa' so that the yaa' could be assimilated into it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 9:

﴿Qāla﴾ (He said): the matter is ﴿kadhālika﴾ (thus), concerning the creation of a boy from you both. ﴿Qāla rabbuka huwa ʿalayya hayyin﴾ (Your Lord said: "It is easy for Me"), i.e., He willed for you the power of intercourse and opened the womb of your wife for conception. ﴿Wa-qad khalaqtuka min qabl wa-lam taku shayʾan﴾ (And I created you before, when you were nothing), before your creation. And to show God's great power, He inspired him to ask, so that he would be answered with what indicates it; and because his soul yearned for the speedy fulfilment of the good news given to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 10:

﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾ That is, a sign of my wife's pregnancy. ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people﴾ for ﴿three nights﴾ (i.e., three days with their nights), as in Surah Al 'Imran, "three days," ﴿while you are sound.﴾ (sawiyyan) is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of tukallim (you speak), meaning: without any impediment.

{Fakharaja ʿalā qawmihi min al-miḥrāb}: "So he came out to his people from the prayer-niche (al-miḥrāb)." That is, the masjid, and they had been waiting for it to be opened so that they could pray in it, by his command, as was customary.

﴿فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا﴾ "So he signalled to them to glorify [God] in the morning and the evening." Awhā (he signalled, indicated) — ishārah — "that glorify": ṣallū (pray). "In the morning and in the evening": the early and the late parts of the day, as was customary.

So he understood, from his being prevented from speaking to them, that she had conceived him (i.e., Yaḥyā), and two years after his birth God the Exalted said to him:

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 19, verse 12:

﴿O Yahya, take the Book﴾ i.e., the Tawrah (Torah) ﴿with strength﴾ with earnestness ﴿And We gave him the judgment﴾ i.e., prophethood (nubuwwah) ﴿as a child﴾ a boy of three years old.

And tenderness (ḥanānan) from Us, meaning mercy towards people, from Our presence (min ladunnā), meaning from Our side, and purity (zakāh), meaning charity to them, and he was pious (taqiyyan). It is related that he never committed a sin and never even intended one.
﴿And dutiful to his parents﴾, i.e., kind to them, ﴿and he was not a tyrant﴾, arrogant, ﴿disobedient﴾, one who disobeys his Lord.

"And peace" from Us "upon him, the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive" (﴿Wa salamun﴾ minna ﴿alayhi yawma wulida wa yawma yamootu wa yawma yubʿathu hayyan﴾). That is: on these fearful days, in which he sees what he had not seen before, so he is safe in them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 16:

﴿And mention in the Book﴾ the Qur'an ﴿Maryam﴾, i.e., her story ﴿when﴾ at the time when ﴿she withdrew from her family to a place facing east﴾, i.e., she secluded herself in a place toward the east of the house.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 17:

﴿So she took a screen apart from them﴾ she let down a curtain to conceal herself behind it, either to delouse her head or her clothes, or to wash from her menstruation. ﴿Then We sent to her Our Spirit﴾ Jibril. ﴿And he appeared to her as a man in every way well-formed﴾ complete in creation, after she had put on her clothes.
﴿She said, "I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ So that you will desist from me because of my seeking refuge.
He said, "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy" with prophethood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 20:

﴿She said, "How can I have a boy when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?"﴾ [i.e., by marriage]; ﴿and I have not been unchaste﴾, meaning a fornicatrix (zaniyah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 21:

﴿He said: "So it will be."﴾ The matter is ﴿thus﴾: the creation of a boy from you without a father. ﴿Your Lord said: "It is easy for Me."﴾ That is: by His command, Jibril will blow into you, and you will conceive him. Since what has been mentioned carries the meaning of a reason (ʿillah), He joined to it ﴿and that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ of Our power, ﴿and a mercy from Us﴾ for whoever believes in him. ﴿And it was a matter decreed﴾ concerning him in My knowledge. So Jibril blew into the opening of her garment, and she felt the child in her womb, formed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 22:

﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place﴾ withdrew (تَنَحَّتْ) ﴿with him to a remote place﴾ far (بَعِيدًا) from her family.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 23:

﴿So the pains of childbirth drove her﴾ brought her [the pangs] ﴿to the trunk of a palm tree﴾ so that she might lean upon it. She gave birth, and the conception, the formation, and the birth occurred within a single hour. ﴿She said: "Oh!"﴾ (yā is used to alert the listener), ﴿"Would that I had died before this"﴾ matter, ﴿"and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten"﴾ a thing discarded, not known and not remembered.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 24:

﴿Then he called to her from beneath her﴾, i.e., Jibril, who was below her. ﴿"Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream."﴾ A river of water that had dried up.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 25:

﴿And shake towards yourself the trunk of the palm-tree﴾ it was dry, and the bāʾ (ب) is extra (zāʾida). ﴿It will drop upon you﴾ its original form was with two tāʾs (تاءان); the second tā' was changed into a sīn and assimilated into the (following) sīn. In another reading it is recited without that (assimilation), ﴿fresh dates﴾ is a specification (tamyīz). ﴿Ripe﴾ is its attribute (ṣifa).

"So eat" from the fresh dates, "and drink" from the stream, "and be consoled" in your eye regarding the child. This is a tamyiz transformed from the subject, meaning: so that your eye may be cooled by him, that is, so that it may be at rest and not crave anything else. "Then if" — here the nun of in (the conditional particle) is assimilated into the extra ma. "You see" — the verb's final radical and its middle radical have been deleted from it, its vowel has been transferred to the rā', and the ya' of the pronoun has been kasrah-ed to avoid the meeting of two sukūns. "Any human being," so that he asks you about your son. "Then say: I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast" — that is, abstention from speech concerning his affair and other matters with people, as evidenced by: "So I will not speak today to any human being," that is, from then on.

﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him﴾ (this is a circumstantial clause, حال). ﴿When they saw him, they said: "O Maryam, you have certainly brought a thing monstrous (فريا)"﴾, meaning a great thing, since you have brought a child without a father.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 28:

﴿O sister of Harun﴾ he was a righteous man, meaning: O one resembling him in chastity. ﴿Your father was not a man of evil﴾, meaning: a fornicator. ﴿Nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, meaning: a fornicatress. So from where did you get this child?
﴿So she pointed﴾ to them toward him, [meaning, to speak to him] ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is﴾ [i.e., who has come into existence] ...

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 30:

﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book"﴾ i.e., the Gospel (al-Injil).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 19, verse 31:**

﴿And He made me blessed wherever I am﴾ i.e., a benefit to people. This is a report of what was decreed for him. ﴿And enjoined upon me prayer and zakat﴾ commanded me to perform them.

[And (He has made me) dutiful to my mother] — object (manṣūb) of a supplied (muqaddar) "jaʿalanī" (He made me).

[And He has not made me a tyrant (jabbār)] — proudly self-exalting (mutaʿāẓiman).

[Wretched (shaqiyyan)] — disobedient to his Lord (ʿāṣiyan li-rabbihi).
[And peace] from God [be] upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive. What was said earlier about the master Yahya applies to it.

**﴿That is ʿĪsā, the son of Maryam, the word of truth﴾**. With the nominative (*bi-l-raf'*, بِالرَّفْع), it is the predicate (*khabar*) of an implied subject (*mubtada' muqaddar*, a subject that is understood but not stated), meaning: "the saying of Ibn Maryam." With the accusative (*bi-l-nasb*, بِالنَّصْب), the verb *qult* ("I say") is understood, and the meaning is: "I say the word of truth."

**﴿the word of truth about which they dispute﴾**: *yamtarūn* comes from *al-miryah* (المِرْيَة), meaning they doubt. **They** are the Christians, who said that ʿĪsā is the son of Allah. **They have lied.**

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 35:

﴿It is not for Allah to take a son; glory be to Him!﴾ (He is exalted above that.) ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (That is, when He wills to bring it into existence.) ﴿So He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ With the nominative (fa-yakūnu, "and it is") by supposing "huwa" (it), and with the accusative by supposing "an" (that). Among that is the creation of Jesus without a father.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 36:

﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.﴾ With the opening of "inna" (wa-inna, "and indeed") according to the supposed verb "udhkur" (remember), and with its kasra (inna) according to the supposed verb "qul" (say), as evidenced by ﴿I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ ﴿This﴾, the aforementioned, is a ﴿path﴾, a way, ﴿straight﴾, leading to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 37:

﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, i.e., the Christians, concerning ʿĪsā (Jesus): was he the son of God, or a god along with Him, or the third of three? ﴿So woe﴾, i.e., severe punishment, ﴿to those who disbelieved﴾ in what has been mentioned and other than it, ﴿from the scene of a tremendous day﴾, i.e., the presence on the Day of Resurrection and its terrors.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 38:

﴿How keen their hearing and how keen their sight will be﴾. Here "bihim" is in the form of two expressions of wonder, meaning "how keen their hearing is!" and "how keen their sight is!" ﴿on the Day they come to Us﴾, in the Hereafter. ﴿But the wrongdoers today﴾, this is the placing of the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun, ﴿are in clear error﴾, i.e., in the world, clearly. By it they were deaf to hearing the truth and blind to seeing it. That is: marvel at them, O addressee, in their hearing and their sight in the Hereafter, after they were deaf and blind in the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 39:

﴿And warn them﴾ (of the Day of Regret), O Muhammad, frighten the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿of the Day of Regret﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, on which the wrongdoer will regret having abandoned good deeds in the world ﴿when the matter will be decided﴾ for them, that they will be punished therein, ﴿while they are﴾ in the world ﴿in heedlessness﴾ of it ﴿and they do not believe﴾ in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾ — "Indeed, it is We" is an emphasis (ta'kid). ﴿And whoever is upon it﴾ — of the rational beings and others — by causing them to perish. ﴿And to Us they will be returned﴾ — for the recompense (al-jaza').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 41:

﴿And mention﴾ to them ﴿in the Book Abraham﴾, i.e., his story, ﴿indeed he was a man of truth﴾, exaggerating in truthfulness, ﴿a prophet﴾. And it is substituted for "his story" (yubdal min khabarihi).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 42:

﴿When he said to his father﴾ Azar, ﴿"O my father"﴾ The "ta" (tā') is a substitute for the "ya" (yā') of possession (iḍāfah), and the two cannot be combined; and he was worshipping idols. ﴿"Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, nor can avail you anything"﴾ i.e., does not suffice you ﴿"in any way"﴾ of benefit or harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 43:

﴿O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a path﴾ a way, ﴿even and straight﴾ upright, straight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 44:

﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾ by your obedience to him in the worship of idols, ﴿indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient﴾ (ʿaṣiyyan), i.e., greatly disobedient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 45:

﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you﴾ if you do not repent, ﴿so you would become a companion (waliyyan) of Satan﴾ — a helper and a close associate to him in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 46:

﴿Said he: "Do you turn away from my gods, Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so beware of me, and leave me for a long time."﴾ Thus you disparage them, ﴿If you do not desist﴾ from opposing them, ﴿I will surely stone you﴾ with stones, or with foul speech; so beware of me, ﴿and leave me for a long time﴾, a long period of time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 47:

﴿He said: "Peace be upon you."﴾ From me, meaning: I will not afflict you with anything you dislike. ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me.﴾ From hafiyy, meaning barr (kind, gracious), so He answers my supplication; and He has fulfilled His promise mentioned in al-Shu'ara' (the Poets). ﴿And forgive my father.﴾ This was before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as He mentioned in Bara'ah (al-Tawbah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 48:

﴿And I will withdraw from you and what you invoke⦆ instead of Allah, meaning what you worship ﴿besides Allah. And I will invoke﴾ I will worship ﴿my Lord. Perhaps I will not be﴾ that I will not be ﴿in my invocation of my Lord﴾ in His worship ﴿unfortunate﴾ as you have been unfortunate by worshipping the idols.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 49:

﴿So when he withdrew from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah﴾ by going to the Holy Land, ﴿We gave him﴾ two sons, with whom he found companionship: ﴿Isaac and Jacob. And each﴾ of them

﴿And We bestowed upon them﴾, meaning the three (Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub), ﴿of Our mercy﴾, meaning wealth and offspring, ﴿and We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾, meaning elevated, which is good praise among all the people of the religions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 51:

﴿And mention in the Book Moses; indeed he was chosen﴾ with the lām pronounced with a kasra and with a fatha, from akhlaṣa (to be sincere, devoted) in his worship, and Allah purified him (khallaṣahu) from defilement.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 52:

﴿And We called him﴾ with the words ﴿"O Moses, indeed I am Allah"﴾ ﴿from the right side of the mount﴾, the name of a mountain, ﴿al-Ayman﴾, i.e., the one that was on the right of Moses when he came from Madyan. ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾, conversing privately, in that Allah made him hear His speech.

﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy,﴾ meaning Our blessing, ﴿his brother Harun﴾ as a substitute (*badal*) or an explicative apposition (*ʿaṭf bayān*), ﴿as a prophet﴾. The word "نَبِيًّا" (*nabiyyan*) is a circumstantial accusative (*ḥāl*). It is the main purpose of the gift, in answer to his request that his brother be sent with him, and Harun was older than him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 54:

﴿And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was true to his promise.﴾ He did not promise anything except that he fulfilled it, and he waited for the one who had promised him, three days or a year, until he came back to him in his place. ﴿And he was a messenger﴾ to Jurhum.

﴿And he used to enjoin his family﴾, meaning his people, ﴿to observe the prayer (ṣalāh) and to give zakāh, and he was ﴿pleasing to his Lord﴾.' Its original form was مَرْضُوّ, and the two wāws were changed into two yāʾs, and the ḍammah became a kasrah.

And mention in the Book Idris. He is the grandfather of Noah's father.

Note: The Arabic commentary says "جَدّ أبِي نُوح", which literally means "the grandfather of Noah's father" (i.e., the father of Noah's father). Following the text as given, the translation reads as above.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 57:

﴿And We raised him to a lofty station.﴾ He is alive in the fourth heaven, or the sixth, or the seventh, or in Paradise, having entered it after being made to taste death and then brought back to life, and he did not leave it.

﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ (those) is a *mubtada'* (subject of a nominal sentence). ﴿الَّذِينَ أنْعَمَ اللَّه عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (those upon whom Allah bestowed favour) is a *sifah* (qualifier, adjective) of it. ﴿مِن النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ (of the prophets) is a *bayan* (clarification, apposition) of it, and it has the meaning of a qualifier. What follows up to the conditional clause is a qualifier of "the prophets." So His saying ﴿مِن ذُرِّيَّة آدَم﴾ (of the offspring of Adam), i.e., Idris. ﴿ومِمَّنْ حَمَلْنا مَعَ نُوح﴾ (and of those We carried with Noah) in the ark, i.e., Ibrahim, the son of his son Sam. ﴿ومِن ذُرِّيَّة إبْراهِيم﴾ (and of the offspring of Abraham), i.e., Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub. ﴿و﴾ (and) of the offspring of ﴿إسْرائِيل﴾ (Israel), who is Ya'qub, i.e., Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa. ﴿ومِمَّنْ هَدَيْنا واجْتَبَيْنا﴾ (and of those whom We guided and chose), i.e., from among them. And the best of those is ﴿إذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آيات الرَّحْمَن خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وبُكِيًّا﴾ (when the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping). *Sujjadan* is the plural of *sajid* (one who prostrates), and *bukiyyan* is the plural of *baki* (one who weeps), i.e., "so be like them." The original form of *bukiyy* is *bukuwy*, in which the waw was changed to ya and the damma to kasra.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 59:

﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires﴾ by abandoning it, like the Jews and the Christians; ﴿and they followed their desires﴾ of sins; ﴿so they will meet with Ghayy﴾, which is a valley in Hell, meaning they will fall into it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 19, verse 60:

﴿Except﴾ but ﴿those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged﴾ in the least, ﴿anything﴾ of their reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 61:

﴿Gardens of Eden⦆ — "Iqāmah" is a substitute (badal) for "al-Jannah" (the Garden). ﴿Which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen﴾, i.e., while absent from them. ﴿Indeed, His promise was⦆, i.e., His promised thing, ﴿coming to pass﴾, in the sense of "ātiyan" (coming), and its original form is "ma'tūwan." Or His promised thing here is the Garden, to which its people come.

They shall not hear therein any idle talk (lagw) ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْوًا﴾ from speech, ﴿except﴾ i.e. but they shall hear ﴿peace﴾ from the angels to them, or from one another to one another, ﴿and they shall have their provision therein morning and evening﴾ i.e. in the measure of those two times in the world. There is no day or night in Paradise, but light and radiance, always.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 19, verse 63:**

﴿That is the Garden which We shall cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was mindful of Us﴾ We give and bestow, ﴿from Our servants whoever was mindful of Us﴾ through his obedience to Him. It was revealed when the revelation (*wahy*) was delayed for days. The Prophet ﷺ said to Jibril: "What prevents you from visiting us more than you visit us?"

We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us (ahead of us, i.e., matters of the Hereafter), and what is behind us (matters of this world), and what is between that (i.e., what happens in this time until the Hour arrives). To Him belongs knowledge of all of it. And your Lord was never forgetful (nasiyyan, in the sense of nasiyan): He did not abandon you by delaying the revelation from you.

He is the Lord (rabb), the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. So worship Him, and be steadfast in His worship. That is, persevere in it. "Do you know of any namesake for Him?" — one who is named with that name? No.

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 66:

﴿And the human being says﴾ — the one who denies the Resurrection, Ubayy ibn Khalaf or al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, the verse having been revealed concerning him — ﴿"When I am dead, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?"﴾ — from the grave, as Muhammad (ﷺ) says. The interrogative here carries the meaning of negation, i.e., "I will not be revived after death." The particle "ma" is additional, for emphasis, and likewise the lam. [The second hamza in the word "a-idha" may be pronounced fully (tahqiq) or eased (tashil), with an alif inserted between it and the other hamza in both of its forms.] He was answered with His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Does not man remember?﴾ Its original form is يَتَذَكَّر (yatadhakkar, "he remembers"): the taa' was changed into a dhaal and merged into the following dhaal. In another recitation (qira'a), the taa' is left unchanged, the dhaal is marked with a sukun, and the kaf takes a damma. ﴿That We created him before, when he was nothing?﴾ Thus, from the beginning of creation, one may infer the possibility of re-creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 68:

﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them﴾ i.e., those who deny the Resurrection, ﴿and the devils﴾ i.e., We will gather each of them along with his devil in a chain. ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell﴾ from outside it, ﴿on their knees﴾ (judhiyyan), the plural of jathin, and its origin is juthuww or juthuy, from jatha yajthu or yajthi, which are two dialects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 69:

﴿Then We will surely drag out from every sect﴾ a group of them ﴿those who were most insolent against the Most Merciful﴾ in defiance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 70:

﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of it [to] burn therein.﴾ [They are] most deserving of Hellfire, the most severe [of them] and others besides them, ﴿to burn therein﴾ by entering it and being burned. So We will begin with them. Its original form is ṣulawiyy, from ṣaliya (with the vowel of the lam either kasra or fatḥa).

"And there is not one of you" — i.e., there is not any of you ﴿except that he will approach it﴾ — i.e., will enter Hell — ﴿it is a decree upon your Lord, [already] decreed and determined﴾ — He decreed it and ruled by it; He will not abandon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 72:

﴿Then We will deliver﴾ (read with shaddah and without shaddah) ﴿those who feared Allah﴾ from it, [i.e., those who were wary of] shirk (associating partners with Allah) and kufr (disbelief) ﴿and We will leave the wrongdoers﴾ in [the state of] shirk and kufr ﴿therein, kneeling﴾ upon their knees.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 73:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., to the believers and the disbelievers, ﴿Our verses﴾ from the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾, evident, as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). ﴿Those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Which of the two groups﴾, we or you, ﴿is better in station﴾, in dwelling and residence, (maqāman) with a fatḥah from qāma (to stand) and with a ḍammah from aqāma (to reside), ﴿and better in assembly?﴾ (nadiyyan), in the sense of al-nādī, which is the gathering place of the people where they converse, meaning: we, so we are better than you."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 74:

﴿How many﴾ i.e., many a one. ﴿We destroyed before them of generations﴾ i.e., of the nations of the past. ﴿Who were better in equipage﴾ in wealth and goods, ﴿and in appearance﴾ in outward appearance, from ru'ya (sight). So just as We destroyed them for their disbelief, We shall destroy these.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 75:

﴿Say: "Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension."﴾ The conditional (sharṭ) whose response (jawāb) is ﴿let him extend﴾, which is in the sense of a statement (khabar), i.e., He extends for him ﴿the Most Merciful extends for him an extension﴾ in this world, leading him on gradually (yastadrijuhu), ﴿until, when they see what they are promised: either the punishment,﴾ such as killing and captivity, ﴿or the Hour,﴾ which encompasses Hell, so they enter it. ﴿Then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in forces﴾ (junud), i.e., helpers: is it they or the believers? Their forces are the devils, and the forces of the believers against them are the angels.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 76:

﴿And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided﴾ by faith, ﴿guidance﴾ through what is sent down to them of the verses. ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾ are obedience, which remains for its doer, ﴿are better with your Lord in reward and better in return﴾, meaning in what is returned to and what one goes back to, unlike the deeds of the disbelievers. The word "better" here is in contrast to their saying: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in position﴾.

﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs﴾: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil. ﴿And said﴾ to Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, who was the one saying to him that you will be resurrected after death, and who was demanding money from him: ﴿I will surely be given wealth and children﴾, on the supposition of the resurrection, ﴿then I will pay you﴾ (your debt).

﴿Has he looked into the unseen?﴾ That is, has he known it, and that he should be given what he has said. The interrogative hamza (hamzat al-istifham) was used in place of the connective hamza (hamzat al-wasl), so the connective hamza was dropped, which is why the word appears as اطّلع rather than اِطّلع. ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ By which he should be given what he has said.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 79:

﴿Kallā﴾ (No!), meaning: that will not be given to him. ﴿Sanaktubu﴾ (We shall record), meaning: We command the recording of ﴿mā yaqūlu﴾ (what he says), ﴿wa-numuddu lahu mina l-ʿadhābi maddā﴾ (and We shall lengthen for him of the punishment an extension), meaning: We will increase him thereby in punishment upon punishment for his disbelief.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 80:**

﴿And We shall inherit from him what he says﴾, of wealth and children; ﴿and he will come to Us﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿alone﴾, having no wealth and no children.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 81:

﴿And they took﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿besides Allah﴾ i.e., the idols, ﴿gods﴾ whom they worship, ﴿that they might be for them a source of might﴾ i.e., intercessors with Allah, so that they would not be punished.

﴿Nay﴾, i.e., there is no preventing their punishment. ﴿They will disavow﴾, i.e., the deities will disavow ﴿their worship﴾, i.e., they will deny it, as in another verse: ﴿they did not worship us﴾. ﴿And they will be against them﴾, i.e., helpers and enemies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 83:

﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them intensely?﴾ That is, We have empowered them over the disbelievers, ﴿inciting them intensely﴾, that is, stirring them up toward sins.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 19, verse 84:

﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾ in seeking the punishment, ﴿for We are only counting for them﴾ the days and nights, or the breaths, ﴿a counting﴾ until the time of their punishment.
Remember (the Day). Remember the Day when We shall gather the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), by their faith, ﴿to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, plural of wafid, meaning: riding.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 19, verse 86:

﴿And We drive the criminals﴾ because of their disbelief ﴿to Hell as a thirsty herd﴾ (wirdan), the plural of wārid, meaning walking and thirsty.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 87:

﴿They shall not have intercession﴾, i.e., the people will not possess intercession, ﴿except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and there is no power nor strength except by Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 88:

﴿And they say﴾ i.e., the Jews and the Christians, and whoever claimed that the angels are daughters of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 89:

﴿Indeed you have produced a thing monstrous﴾, i.e., a grave abomination.

﴿Nearly﴾ read with the ta' and with the ya': ﴿the heavens are nearly splitting﴾ read with the ta' and with the shaddah on the ṭā', meaning "splitting asunder," and in one recitation (qirā'a) with the nūn: ﴿from Him﴾, ﴿and the earth is split open and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾. That is, they fall upon them ﴿because they ascribed a son to the Most Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 92:

﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ i.e., it is not becoming of Him to do so.

﴿In﴾, meaning "not": ﴿there is none in the heavens and the earth but he will come to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾, humbled and submissive, on the Day of Resurrection. Among them are ʿUzayr and ʿIsa.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 94:

﴿He has indeed enumerated them and counted them with exact counting.﴾ So the total number of all of them is not hidden from Him, nor is any single one of them.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 95:**

﴿And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ without wealth and without any helper for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 19, verse 96:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾, among themselves. They love one another and are loved, and Allah the Exalted loves them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 97:

﴿Indeed, We have made it easy﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿in your tongue﴾ the Arabic, ﴿so that you may give good tidings thereby to the God-fearing﴾ those who succeed through faith, ﴿and warn thereby a people obstinate﴾ you may frighten thereby, ﴿lud﴾ is the plural of alad, i.e., those who argue falsely, and they are the disbelievers of Makkah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 19, verse 98:

﴿And how many﴾ i.e., many. ﴿We destroyed before them of a generation﴾ i.e., a nation of the past nations, because of their denial of the messengers. ﴿Do you perceive of them anyone or hear from them a sound?﴾ i.e., do you find of them any one, or hear from them a faint sound? No. Just as We destroyed those, We shall destroy these.
